name: Application sidebar rail (compact mode)
purpose: A middle state between the full application sidebar and the mobile drawer: a 56px icon rail for pages that need the width, such as a workspace. It is the same single navigation list, not a second sidebar.
whenToUse: A workspace or canvas page needs the horizontal room and the person knows the icons.
The application has a stable set of areas with recognizable icons from the catalog.
The person should be able to choose the width, with the route supplying a default.
whenNotToUse: Pages that read like documents or settings, where labels help. Default those routes to expanded.
Applications whose areas have no clear icon. A rail of ambiguous icons is worse than labels.
Mobile widths (820px and below). The sidebar is a drawer there and always shows labels.
A second navigation column beside the sidebar (P14). The rail replaces the width, it never adds a column.
anatomy: Rail: 56px wide, the same surface as the expanded sidebar (--s0).
Brand mark only; the name is visually hidden.
Navigation items: 16px icon centered, label visually hidden but in the accessibility tree, title attribute as tooltip.
Width toggle at the bottom: chevrons icon, label Expand navigation or Collapse navigation.

variants.description: Icon and label, 252px (224px in some applications).

variants.useWhen: Workspace routes by default, or when the person chooses it.

behavior: Mode is chosen by the route and an explicit choice always wins. Store the choice as null (route decides) or a boolean.
Below 820px the sidebar is the existing drawer and ignores the compact mode.
Active item uses the existing aria-current treatment (P15, P17).
accessibility: Labels are never display:none, so every item keeps its accessible name in the rail.
The width toggle has aria-pressed and a label that names the action.
Targets: 32px high on desktop, at least 40px effective on touch and coarse pointers (the shared hit-area rule).
Tooltips come from the title attribute; they are a convenience, not the only name.
statusNote: Candidate for PR-0002, not part of any approved bundle. Whether the rail needs its own preset or is a variant of a future application shell preset is an owner decision.
